bull.b: Neffy is gaining adoption in the U.S., with market share doubling year over year. Continued prescriber growth and focused deployment of the sales force could support durable penetration in the anaphylaxis market.

A rapidly expanding prescriber base broadens the commercial foundation for neffy and reduces dependence on a small group of early adopters. This supports repeat demand and may improve operating leverage as the product becomes more established.

Strong product-level gross margins provide a foundation for eventual profitability, while planned expense reductions address the current cost imbalance. Successful execution could extend liquidity and move the business toward management's breakeven target.

bear.b: Losses remain far larger than the current revenue base, showing that commercial growth has not yet translated into earnings. Sustained operating deficits increase the risk that additional financing or dilution will be needed before scale benefits emerge.

The company is not yet funding operations internally, and cash consumption remains substantial despite some improvement from the prior annual period. Continued burn could shorten the financial runway and constrain investment in commercialization and pipeline programs.

A sharply reduced equity cushion makes the capital structure vulnerable while losses and cash burn persist. High leverage limits financial flexibility and raises refinancing or dilution risk if the planned path to cash-flow breakeven is delayed.
